ai_diagnosis: DNS resolution failure: PC cannot resolve external hosts. Update DNS to 8.8.8.8.
corrected_diagnosis: Client default gateway (192.168.20.1) is outside the local subnet (192.168.10.0/24).
reason_ai_was_wrong: The AI focused on the higher-layer symptom ('cannot reach Internet') without checking foundational Layer 3 subnet membership.
evidence_used: ipconfig /all shows host IP 192.168.10.25/24 with default gateway 192.168.20.1 in another subnet.
lesson: Always troubleshoot networking from bottom to top (Layer 1-3 before Layer 7 DNS). An unreachable gateway invalidates off-subnet DNS queries.

ai_diagnosis: Upstream ISP WAN gateway is unresponsive or experiencing a provider outage.
corrected_diagnosis: DHCP pool default-router option has a typo (192.168.1.254 instead of 192.168.1.1).
reason_ai_was_wrong: The AI jumped to blaming an external ISP outage rather than inspecting local DHCP scope parameters in the running config.
evidence_used: show running-config shows 'default-router 192.168.1.254' on router R1 whose actual LAN IP is 192.168.1.1.
lesson: Verify local configuration and DHCP options before assuming upstream service provider faults.

ai_diagnosis: NAT translation failure: The router has no active dynamic NAT mappings to translate LAN traffic.
corrected_diagnosis: Edge router R1 has no default route (Gateway of last resort is not set).
reason_ai_was_wrong: The AI confused NAT failure with missing routing. In Cisco IOS, routing precedes NAT; without a default route, packets are discarded before translation.
evidence_used: show ip route explicitly states 'Gateway of last resort is not set' with no 0.0.0.0/0 route.
lesson: A router cannot translate or forward packets to unknown networks without a valid route. Routing comes before NAT in packet flow.

ai_diagnosis: 802.1Q Inter-VLAN Trunking failure: Switch-1 trunk port is failing to forward VLAN 20 frames.
corrected_diagnosis: Standard ACL 10 outbound on subinterface Gi0/0.20 blocks PC 192.168.10.10 via implicit deny.
reason_ai_was_wrong: The AI hypothesized a Layer 2 trunking failure without checking the provided ACL output which showed 87 implicit deny matches.
evidence_used: show access-lists 10 shows 'permit 192.168.10.5' and '(implicit deny any matches: 87)' blocking host 192.168.10.10.
lesson: Counter matches on ACL deny statements are conclusive proof of packet filtering; do not invent Layer 2 trunking faults when Layer 3/4 filtering is evident.

ai_diagnosis: WAN Serial interface link failure: Upstream WAN provider link line protocol is down.
corrected_diagnosis: WAN interface GigabitEthernet0/1 is missing the 'ip nat outside' configuration statement.
reason_ai_was_wrong: The AI hallucinated a physical link down condition when the show output clearly stated Gi0/1 was up, missing the NAT domain configuration error.
evidence_used: show running-config interface Gi0/1 shows no 'ip nat outside', and 'show ip nat statistics' reports Outside interfaces: None.
lesson: AI models can exhibit confirmation bias toward physical failures. Human reviewers must check interface state counters against configuration evidence.

ai_diagnosis: Wi-Fi WPA2 pre-shared key compromise: Unauthorized guest client obtained corporate Wi-Fi credentials.
corrected_diagnosis: Guest Wi-Fi subinterface (Gi0/0.99) lacks an ACL to restrict guest traffic from private corporate subnets.
reason_ai_was_wrong: The AI assumed an encryption/authentication issue rather than recognizing that default inter-VLAN routing forwards packets between all router subinterfaces unless restricted.
evidence_used: show running-config interface Gi0/0.99 shows no ip access-group, and show access-lists confirms no guest isolation ACL exists.
lesson: Inter-VLAN routing is enabled by default across router subinterfaces; security boundaries between guest and internal networks require explicit Layer 3/4 ACL filtering.
